stem: Organisms too small to be seen with the naked eye are called __________.
solution: Microorganisms are tiny living things visible only under a microscope.

stem: The instrument used to observe microorganisms is the __________.
solution: A microscope magnifies tiny objects, allowing microorganisms to be seen.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a major group of microorganisms?
solution: Bacteria, fungi, protozoa (and algae) are microorganisms; mammals are large animals.

stem: The microorganisms that lie on the borderline of living and non-living and reproduce only inside a host are __________.
solution: Viruses reproduce only inside a living host and are considered on the border of living and non-living.

stem: Curd is formed from milk by the action of __________.
solution: Bacteria (Lactobacillus) convert milk into curd by fermentation.

stem: The rising of bread dough is caused by __________, which releases carbon dioxide.
solution: Yeast, a fungus, ferments sugar producing CO₂ that makes the dough rise.

stem: The process by which microorganisms break down sugars to produce alcohol or acids is called __________.
solution: Fermentation is the breakdown of sugars by microorganisms, yielding products like alcohol and acids.

stem: Diseases caused by microorganisms are called __________ diseases.
solution: Infectious (communicable) diseases are caused by microorganisms and can spread.

stem: Malaria is caused by a __________ transmitted by the Anopheles mosquito.
solution: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium, spread by the female Anopheles mosquito.

stem: Which of these diseases is caused by a virus?
solution: The common cold is viral; tuberculosis, typhoid and cholera are bacterial.

stem: Tuberculosis is caused by a __________.
solution: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease affecting mainly the lungs.

stem: An organism that carries a disease-causing microbe from one host to another is called a __________.
solution: A vector, such as a mosquito, carries pathogens from one host to another.

stem: A substance that provides immunity against a disease by preparing the body's defence is a __________.
solution: A vaccine trains the body's immune system to fight a particular disease.

stem: Medicines that kill or stop the growth of disease-causing bacteria are called __________.
solution: Antibiotics are medicines that destroy or inhibit bacteria.

stem: Antibiotics are NOT effective against __________.
solution: Antibiotics act against bacteria (and some other microbes) but not against viruses.

stem: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria found in the root nodules of leguminous plants convert atmospheric nitrogen into __________.
solution: These bacteria fix free nitrogen into compounds that plants can absorb and use.

stem: Microorganisms that break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil, are called __________.
solution: Decomposers recycle nutrients by breaking down dead organic matter.

stem: The process of heating milk to a high temperature briefly and then cooling it quickly to kill harmful microbes is called __________.
solution: Pasteurisation heats and rapidly cools milk to destroy harmful microorganisms.

stem: Adding salt or sugar in large amounts preserves food because it __________.
options: draws out water and checks microbial growth
solution: High salt or sugar removes water by osmosis, preventing microbes from growing.

stem: Storing food at low temperature in a refrigerator preserves it by __________.
options: slowing down the growth of microbes
solution: Cold temperatures slow microbial growth, delaying food spoilage.

stem: Chemicals added to food to prevent spoilage by microbes are called __________.
solution: Preservatives such as salt, sugar and certain chemicals stop microbial spoilage of food.

stem: Which microorganism is used to make antibiotics like penicillin?
solution: Penicillin is produced from the mould Penicillium, a fungus.

stem: Some algae are microscopic and, being green, can carry out __________.
solution: Green algae contain chlorophyll and make food by photosynthesis.

stem: Food poisoning can result from eating food in which harmful __________ have grown.
solution: Harmful microbes multiplying in food can produce toxins causing food poisoning.

stem: A disease that spreads from an infected person to a healthy person is said to be __________.
solution: Communicable diseases spread from person to person through various means.

stem: The spread of disease can be reduced by maintaining __________.
solution: Good hygiene and sanitation limit the spread of disease-causing microbes.

stem: Mosquitoes breed in __________, so removing it helps control mosquito-borne diseases.
solution: Stagnant water is a breeding site for mosquitoes; removing it reduces their numbers.

stem: The body's natural defence system that fights infections is the __________ system.
solution: The immune system defends the body against invading microorganisms.

stem: Which of the following is a beneficial role of microorganisms?
solution: Microorganisms are beneficial in making curd, bread and other foods, among other uses.

stem: Cholera and typhoid spread mainly through __________.
solution: Cholera and typhoid are water- and food-borne bacterial diseases.

stem: The first vaccine, against smallpox, was developed by __________.
solution: Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine, pioneering vaccination.

stem: Penicillin, the first antibiotic, was discovered by __________.
solution: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin from the Penicillium mould.

stem: Microorganisms are used in sewage treatment to __________.
solution: Decomposer microbes break down organic matter in sewage during treatment.

stem: The nitrogen cycle depends on microorganisms that __________.
options: fix nitrogen and recycle nitrogen compounds
solution: Microbes fix atmospheric nitrogen and recycle nitrogen compounds, maintaining the nitrogen cycle.

stem: A microorganism that lives in or on another organism and causes it harm is called a __________.
solution: A pathogen is a disease-causing microorganism.

stem: Boiling drinking water helps make it safe because it __________.
solution: Boiling kills most harmful microorganisms, making water safer to drink.

stem: Which of these is used in the large-scale production of alcohol?
solution: Yeast ferments sugars to produce alcohol on an industrial scale.

stem: The tiny, single-celled animals grouped as protozoa include the causative agent of __________.
solution: The malaria parasite Plasmodium is a protozoan.

stem: Covering the nose and mouth while sneezing helps prevent the spread of __________ diseases.
solution: Airborne diseases spread through droplets; covering the mouth limits their spread.

stem: Fungi such as bread mould grow well in conditions that are __________.
solution: Warm, moist conditions favour the growth of fungi like bread mould.

stem: Which practice does NOT help prevent food spoilage by microbes?
options: Leaving cooked food uncovered in the open
solution: Leaving food uncovered exposes it to microbes and hastens spoilage.

stem: Blue-green algae in fields are useful because they can __________.
solution: Certain blue-green algae fix nitrogen, enriching the soil naturally.

stem: The reason viruses are considered different from other microorganisms is that they __________.
options: can reproduce only inside a living host cell
are visible to the naked eye
solution: Viruses cannot reproduce on their own; they need a living host cell to multiply.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a fungal skin disease?
solution: Ringworm is caused by a fungus and affects the skin.

stem: Vaccination programmes have helped to __________ certain diseases like smallpox.
solution: Widespread vaccination eradicated smallpox and controls many diseases.

stem: The main reason we cannot see bacteria with the naked eye is that they are __________.
solution: Bacteria are far too small to be seen without a microscope.

stem: Which of the following helps to increase soil fertility naturally?
solution: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria enrich the soil with usable nitrogen compounds.

stem: Personal hygiene such as washing hands before eating helps prevent __________.
options: entry of harmful microbes into the body
solution: Washing hands removes microbes, reducing the chance of infection through food.

stem: A community that is largely protected because most of its members are vaccinated shows __________.
solution: Herd immunity protects a population when a large fraction is immune, limiting disease spread.

stem: Overall, microorganisms are best described as __________.
options: both useful and harmful depending on the type
solution: Microorganisms play both beneficial and harmful roles depending on the species and situation.
